types.text: Bit 63 of MSR_PKG_POWER_LIMIT is 0, meaning PL1 is changeable at runtime and reverts on reset.
Node 0's send rate increased by 1.8% (from 3925 to 3997) after the OS change.
The extracted facts achieved 100% recall, matching chunks alone, while using 2.3x fewer context tokens and being 1.7x faster.
The `VCA_VIRTIO_COPY_DESC` ioctl returns `-EFAULT` and is a stub, meaning userspace DMA should not be designed around it.
The driver builds both roles: 18 host-role and 15 node-role modules, including vcablkfe and vcablk_bckend.
KVMGT (GPU slices into VMs) is in the Intel matrix for Ubuntu 16.04 on this card.
The CPU is 1.9x faster since the 22.04 image.
With RPC to node 0 only, the generation time was 30.2 t/s.
Host-push into guest RAM achieves a rate of approximately 3.7 GiB/s.
The `VCA_VIRTIO_COPY_DESC` mechanism is Stubbed with `-EFAULT` in `vop_vringh.c`.
The minimum iteration time for Node 0 was 0.033 ms.
The VCA stack was untouched, and both `vca2-vcass` DKMS entries remained intact.
The card achieves 1.36 TFLOP/s FP32, which is 34% of its 4.0 TFLOP/s paper peak.
The blk-mq conversion is genuine and structural, with `blk_peek_request` / `blk_start_request` / `__blk_end_request_all` absent from the entire fork tree.
ALUT doorbell mailbox on all 3 nodes has a ping of ~35 µs, and host-push into guest RAM is ~3.7 GiB/s.
`reconcile_repair.py` re-judged the store in ~70 short calls (instead of a 72-minute re-ingest) and restored 48 facts.
Guest `alut_gmap.ko` called `plx_add_a_lut_entry(0x4c000000)` with guest `peer_off=0x8000000`.
The mailbox structure has a 512-byte command header at LBA 0 and the payload at 4 KiB.
The topology includes host root port 00:03.2.
Wrapping the body in `<document source="...">` tags fixes the issue with chunks starting with a heading path.
Typical counts for kernel modules affected by this relocation issue are 27–44 relocations each.
The host's RTX 3070 was using `nouveau` for software encoding.
The `vca_mgr_extd` sysfs device was renamed, which breaks anything matching the old name at runtime only.
Only `ubuntu-jammy` is marked as `proven`, meaning it was built, booted, and benchmarked on the hardware.
The iGPU evicts the CPU's working set from the shared eDRAM/LLC.
Submitting several descriptors and flagging on completion callbacks would close the remaining gap to ~4000.
The host's share under the 'both' configuration was 694 fps against 688 fps when running alone, indicating no contention.
The 4462 MiB/s CPU-free ring would not resolve the serialization issue.
The maximum number of doorbells is defined as `PLX_MAXDB 16` in `plx_hw.h`.
The host program `compute/gpu_all3.py` on `vca-host` fires the same OpenCL SAXPY on all three P580s using SSH/TCP (virtio-net) transport.
Verified working modules include `alut_gmap.ko`, `n2n.ko`, and `ring.ko` when built with gcc 11 / binutils 2.38 and patched.
For a test on node 0 with n=1536, rows=512, the performance was 9.27 GFLOP/s.
Each node utilizes an llm running gemma-4-E4B-it Q4_K_M on port 8082.
The aggregate across three nodes was corrected from "99 -> 250" to approximately "109 -> 210 GFLOP/s".

The `spoto-team/vca2-control-panel` is a Python/Flask web UI wrapping `vcactl`, which includes features like power button control, RAMDisk vs BlockIO boot selection, block device attach/detach, network status, and node status visualization.
OLMoE reads 0.6 GB/token, which results in it being 4x faster than a dense 7B model.
jumbo_mtu.ko and hostbuf.ko were rebuilt for 7.0.14.
The best node↔node path reaches 4423 MiB/s pipelined, CPU-free.
For a pure-ALU synthetic load, the `burn` workload pins the package at 43.5-44.6 W.
MSR 0x614 (PKG_POWER_INFO) reports TDP = 45.00 W.
Intel's stock `plx87xx` cannot compile against this kernel because it supplies a `dma_map_ops` table and `.map_page` no longer exists as a member.
The script `compute/image/plt32_to_pc32.py` was written and installed as `/usr/local/sbin/plt32-to-pc32` to rewrite 27–44 relocations per module.
Only GPU+CPU together is cap-bound, reaching 43.5-44.6 W against a 45 W limit.
Host kicks doorbell 15, and the guest IRQ wakes a waiter that acknowledges the header.
The kernel `7.0.2-6-pve` remains installed.
The file `etc/systemd/system/vca-netcfg.service` runs `vca-netcfg.sh` with a timeout long enough for the retry loop.
Node 0's receive rate increased by 1.0% (from 3911 to 3949) after the OS change.
The vca2-card.service boots the nodes at host start and powers them off cleanly at stop.
The CPU work in the combined test showed times of 0.24 s for cpu0, 0.32 s for cpu1, and 0.31 s for cpu2.
Combined throughput across the fabric when running concurrently was 8118 MiB/s.
The host already masquerades `172.31.0.0/16`.
Ingesting 22 documents resulted in 448 chunks and 748 memories in 71.9 minutes.
The parallel ping of all three nodes took approximately 63 ms wall time.
On the working kernel, the vop-dev0* probe lines land approximately 35 seconds after the PLX links come up, which is only after vcactl boot has run.
Each node has one Skylake GT4e, PCI ID 8086:193A, with 128 MB eDRAM.
Host DMA buffer plus a guest A-LUT entry allows each node to mmap BAR2.
The gate for a newer kernel is vcablk, which uses the legacy blk_init_queue request API removed in 5.0 and needs a blk-mq conversion.
The module was built with `-g -gdwarf-5`, and its DWARF `DW_AT_comp_dir` pointed to `/usr/src/vca2-vcass-2.3.26+ubuntu24.04.10`.
Virtio-net TCP achieved speeds of approximately 4.7–5.0 Gbit/s host→node and ~3.5 Gbit/s node→host.
Guest pull of host RAM achieves a rate of approximately 28 MiB/s.
The BlockIO backend runs synchronous DMA, and the async path is dead code.
The transport used is `vca_virtio_net` in Intel's 4.14 kernel, which the new image does not replace.
The correct value for `MAX_COMPUTE_UNITS` is `0x1002`, which returns 72.
The embedder model size is 0.64 GB, and its memory usage decreased from ~5.0 GB to 0.90 GB after optimization.
Point node 0's A-LUT window at the host-domain address of node 1's NTB BAR2 instead of at host RAM.
There is no QPI, no NVLink, and no coherent shared memory between the E3s.
The CPU GEMM n=2048 results were 54.53 on node 0, 53.80 on node 1, and 53.82 on node 2.
When re-measured with all three nodes on one identical image, node 1 achieved a receive rate of 4973 and 4724 when reading from host RAM.
VOP virtio-net + DMA is Real and achieves ~5 Gbit/s TCP.
Host BAR2 at each host peer_off aliases guest kernel RAM.
Two reboots occurred on 7.0.14 with the patched `plx87xx` (srcversion C7DB21AFCC365566F4BFCAA).
For N=1536, the per GPU GFLOP/s values were 1024 for 408, 1408 for 457, and 1536 for 445.
When the Guest `resource2` mmap was performed at `0x22000000`, it mapped but did not hang, reading `0xffffffff`.
With the active cooling fitted ("super-cooler-5000"), the idle temperature dropped from ~40 °C to 35-37 °C.
The guest-side NTB for node 0 has BAR2 set to 4 GB at address `3e00000000` and operates over a Link of 8 GT/s ×8 (PCIe Gen3 x8).
Guest INPUT includes TCP 9200 (OpenCL daemon) and 50052 (llama RPC).
64-byte alignment is required for src, dst and len (`PLX_DMA_ALIGN_SHIFT 6`) for optimal performance.
Keep batches to ~32 docs at 2048 context.
With all three nodes running AVX2, cores reached 92-94 °C under stock airflow.
Host writes the ALUT header and kicks db 15, spinning on `status==2`.
Handing the extractor a chunk starting `THERMAL.md > ...` made the model reply "Please provide the content of THERMAL.md so I can extract the durable facts."
Authentication is off by default, but it can be required on every `/v*` route by starting the server with `SMEM_TOKEN=<secret>`.
The harness now writes `bakeoff-results.json` before formatting anything, including every extracted fact.
Trip at 85 °C, not 88, because the observed overshoot between samples was 4-6 °C.
Dropping the package limit to ~35 W would cap the AVX2 case well below 96 °C at a modest performance cost.
The recommended sizes to use are 1024, 640, or 1408, and 1536 should not be used.
The best operating range for the tuned kernel is N = 1024..2048; N=3072 drops to 256 GFLOP/s as the working set outgrows the cache.
The bake-off verdict was to stay on gemma-4-E4B.
Tensor parallelism could suit the fabric well, with activations around 8 KB/token/layer and a ~35 µs doorbell implying a ~450 tok/s ceiling.
The host-side engine is 1.7x SLOWER (~2300 MiB/s) for the identical transfer, and it is recommended to always initiate bulk DMA from the card side.
A newer kernel is not worth losing 4423 MiB/s node-to-node.
The host kernel pin is unnecessary.
Editing `PKGS_BASE` is a footgun if you rely on the cache for a clean bootstrap.
Changing `PKGS_*` in a profile requires deleting `$WORK/rootfs-<profile>/` to get a clean bootstrap.
The builder assumes the Intel reference image is present.
The builder deliberately disables `systemd-resolved` to prevent the creation of a symlink in `/etc/resolv.conf` on the nodes.
The deploy script refuses to run if the master image is attached anywhere.
The `SUPPORT` field exists so the repo cannot quietly imply a profile works when nobody has booted it.
Anything reported upstream should name the local `plx87xx` patch because the team has validated the port plus a modification.
Verify copied models by SIZE, not existence, by comparing `stat -c%s` against the source.
To recover a node whose sshd is dead, do NOT reach for `vcactl reset --force`.
If NICs are missing, one should check `vcactl status` first, as `bios_up` means nobody booted the nodes.
To clear the 'REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED' warning after swapping images, use ssh-keygen -f /root/.ssh/known_hosts -R 172.31.N.1.
